author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pip](https://pypi.org/project/pip) from **18.1** to **21.0.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 21.0.1
   ```
   ===================

Bug Fixes
---------

- commands: debug: Use packaging.version.parse to compare between versions. (`9461 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9461>`_)
- New resolver: Download and prepare a distribution only at the last possible
  moment to avoid unnecessary network access when the same version is already
  installed locally. (`9516 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9516>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade packaging to 20.9
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.0
   ```
   =================

Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- Drop support for Python 2. (`6148 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6148>`_)
- Remove support for legacy wheel cache entries that were created with pip
  versions older than 20.0. (`7502 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7502>`_)
- Remove support for VCS pseudo URLs editable requirements. It was emitting
  deprecation warning since version 20.0. (`7554 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7554>`_)
- Modernise the codebase after Python 2. (`8802 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8802>`_)
- Drop support for Python 3.5. (`9189 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9189>`_)
- Remove the VCS export feature that was used only with editable VCS
  requirements and had correctness issues. (`9338 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9338>`_)

Features
--------

- Add ``--ignore-requires-python`` support to pip download. (`1884 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/1884>`_)
- New resolver: Error message shown when a wheel contains inconsistent metadata
  is made more helpful by including both values from the file name and internal
  metadata. (`9186 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9186>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- Fix a regression that made ``pip wheel`` do a VCS export instead of a VCS clone
  for editable requirements. This broke VCS requirements that need the VCS
  information to build correctly. (`9273 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9273>`_)
- Fix ``pip download`` of editable VCS requirements that need VCS information
  to build correctly. (`9337 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9337>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade msgpack to 1.0.2.
- Upgrade requests to 2.25.1.

Improved Documentation
----------------------

- Render the unreleased pip version change notes on the news page in docs. (`9172 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9172>`_)
- Fix broken email link in docs feedback banners. (`9343 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9343>`_)


.. note

    You should *NOT* be adding new change log entries to this file, this
    file is managed by towncrier. You *may* edit previous change logs to
    fix problems like typo corrections or such.

    To add a new change log entry, please see
        https://pip.pypa.io/en/latest/development/contributing/#news-entries

.. towncrier release notes start
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.4
   ```
   ===================

Features
--------

- ``pip wheel`` now verifies the built wheel contains valid metadata, and can be
  installed by a subsequent ``pip install``. This can be disabled with
  ``--no-verify``. (`9206 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9206>`_)
- Improve presentation of XMLRPC errors in pip search. (`9315 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9315>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- Fixed hanging VCS subprocess calls when the VCS outputs a large amount of data
  on stderr. Restored logging of VCS errors that was inadvertently removed in pip
  20.2. (`8876 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8876>`_)
- Fix error when an existing incompatibility is unable to be applied to a backtracked state. (`9180 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9180>`_)
- New resolver: Discard a faulty distribution, instead of quitting outright.
  This implementation is taken from 20.2.2, with a fix that always makes the
  resolver iterate through candidates from indexes lazily, to avoid downloading
  candidates we do not need. (`9203 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9203>`_)
- New resolver: Discard a source distribution if it fails to generate metadata,
  instead of quitting outright. This implementation is taken from 20.2.2, with a
  fix that always makes the resolver iterate through candidates from indexes
  lazily, to avoid downloading candidates we do not need. (`9246 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9246>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade resolvelib to 0.5.4.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.3
   ```
   ===================

Bug Fixes
---------

- Revert "Skip candidate not providing valid metadata", as that caused pip to be overeager about downloading from the package index. (`9264 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9264>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.2
   ```
   ===================

Features
--------

- New resolver: Resolve direct and pinned (``==`` or ``===``) requirements first
  to improve resolver performance. (`9185 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9185>`_)
- Add a mechanism to delay resolving certain packages, and use it for setuptools. (`9249 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9249>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- New resolver: The "Requirement already satisfied" log is not printed only once
  for each package during resolution. (`9117 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9117>`_)
- Fix crash when logic for redacting authentication information from URLs
  in ``--help`` is given a list of strings, instead of a single string. (`9191 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9191>`_)
- New resolver: Correctly implement PEP 592. Do not return yanked versions from
  an index, unless the version range can only be satisfied by yanked candidates. (`9203 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9203>`_)
- New resolver: Make constraints also apply to package variants with extras, so
  the resolver correctly avoids backtracking on them. (`9232 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9232>`_)
- New resolver: Discard a candidate if it fails to provide metadata from source,
  or if the provided metadata is inconsistent, instead of quitting outright. (`9246 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9246>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Update vendoring to 20.8

Improved Documentation
----------------------

- Update documentation to reflect that pip still uses legacy resolver by default in Python 2 environments. (`9269 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9269>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.1
   ```
   ===================

Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- The --build-dir option has been restored as a no-op, to soften the transition
  for tools that still used it. (`9193 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9193>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3
   ```
   - Introduce a new ResolutionImpossible error, raised when pip encounters un-satisfiable dependency conflicts (`8546 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8546>`_, `#8377 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8377>`_)
- Add a subcommand ``debug`` to ``pip config`` to list available configuration sources and the key-value pairs defined in them. (`6741 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6741>`_)
- Warn if index pages have unexpected content-type (`6754 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6754>`_)
- Allow specifying ``--prefer-binary`` option in a requirements file (`7693 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7693>`_)
- Generate PEP 376 REQUESTED metadata for user supplied requirements installed
  by pip. (`7811 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7811>`_)
- Warn if package url is a vcs or an archive url with invalid scheme (`8128 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8128>`_)
- Parallelize network operations in ``pip list``. (`8504 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8504>`_)

This PR updates [packaging](https://pypi.org/project/packaging) from **20.3** to **20.9**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 20.9
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Run `isort <https://pypi.org/project/isort/>`_ over the code base (:issue:`377`)
* Add support for the ``macosx_10_*_universal2`` platform tags (:issue:`379`)
* Introduce ``packaging.utils.parse_wheel_filename()`` and ``parse_sdist_filename()``
  (:issue:`387` and :issue:`389`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.8
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Revert back to setuptools for compatibility purposes for some Linux distros (:issue:`363`)
* Do not insert an underscore in wheel tags when the interpreter version number
  is more than 2 digits (:issue:`372`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.7
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

No unreleased changes.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.6
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

.. note:: This release was subsequently yanked, and these changes were included in 20.7.

* Fix flit configuration, to include LICENSE files (:issue:`357`)
* Make `intel` a recognized CPU architecture for the `universal` macOS platform tag (:issue:`361`)
* Add some missing type hints to `packaging.requirements` (issue:`350`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.5
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Officially support Python 3.9 (:issue:`343`)
* Deprecate the ``LegacyVersion`` and ``LegacySpecifier`` classes (:issue:`321`)
* Handle ``OSError`` on non-dynamic executables when attempting to resolve
  the glibc version string.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.4
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Canonicalize version before comparing specifiers. (:issue:`282`)
* Change type hint for ``canonicalize_name`` to return
  ``packaging.utils.NormalizedName``.
  This enables the use of static typing tools (like mypy) to detect mixing of
  normalized and un-normalized names.
   ```
   
  
</details>

body:
## Description

The way that I set up state management for promotions currently was a bit non-conventional and difficult to maintain. So I thought I should change it to be a bit more like [Redux](https://redux.js.org/tutorials/fundamentals/part-3-state-actions-reducers).

Here's the simple breakdown of how it works and why/when this approach works:
![Screen Shot 2020-12-31 at 9 15 28 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44531733/103433868-ca46e000-4bad-11eb-88e2-329280b9fa34.png)
![Screen Shot 2020-12-31 at 9 15 52 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44531733/103433870-d763cf00-4bad-11eb-9fa6-7d9e37eafe20.png)

So in our app, we can make use of this pattern to manage which promotions are currently being shown and in what order (filtering and sorting) according to which options have been selected for each dropdown. We have three main parts:
- The context provider component in `contexts/PromotionsList.tsx`: 
  - `PromotionsListProvider` component is what is used in the component hierarchy, allowing any of it's child components to make use of the context object (which we can access using the `usePromotionsList` function
- The reducer function in `reducers/PromotionsList.ts`
  - This function is responsible for taking the previous state object, along with the parameters to the dispatch call and constructing the new state. Basically, this function is called whenever you see a call to `dispatch`.
- The components making use of the context: 
  - `DropdownMenu.tsx`: Dropdown menu on the home page, used here because it allows us to clear all filters
  - `PromotionList.tsx`: List of promotions on home page, used here because we need to filter and sort the promotions whenever the state has been updated
  - `Home.tsx`: Home screen, used here because this is where we define the actions for the dropdowns

I've tried to add documentation wherever I could to make it easier to understand, but let me know if I should add some more in certain places. Let me know if there's anything that needs further explanation!

author: jure
body:
**Description**

In `Quaternion.slerp` we return early if `t` is 0 or 1, returning `qa` if `t` 0 and `qb` if `t` 1. We don't do the same in `slerpFlat` and it impacts performance in certain cases.

1.000.000 slerpFlats without early return in msec (using the quats in in `Quaternion.tests.js`):

| t  | time in msec | 
| --------  | ------------------- |
|0| **56.661** |
|1| **60.9848** |
|0.5| 50.9151 |
|0.25| 47.1928 |
|0.75| 47.2224 |
|0.5| 36.2757 |
|0.5| 39.1083 |

1.000.000 slerpFlats with early return:

| t  | time in msec | 
| --------  | ------------------- |
|0 | **12.8091**|
|1 | **14.754**|
|0.5 | 52.2216|
|0.25 | 48.1502|
|0.75 | 47.7769|
|0.5 | 34.5647|
|0.5 | 37.7248|

There is some natural variation, but for `t` 0 and `t` 1 the early return variant is on average 4-5x faster.

In a real world example where `slerpFlat` is used to interpolate between player rotations in a multiplayer scenario, I'm definitely seeing an improvement.

Happy to code golf it a bit more, but I'm looking for feedback on whether the change is appropriate first.

body:
- 記憶トークンと記憶ダイジェストを比較する（`app/models/user.rb`）

```
class User < ApplicationRecord
 ・・・ 
  def authenticated?(remember_token)
    BCrypt::Password.new(remember_digest).is_password?(remember_token)
  end
end
```

記憶トークンと記憶ダイジェストが一致するときに`true`を返す`authenticated?`メソッドを追加。

- ユーザーを記憶する（`app/helpers/sessions_helper.rb`）

```
module SessionsHelper
 ・・・
  def remember(user)
    user.remember
    cookies.permanent.signed[:user_id] = user.id
    cookies.permanent[:remember_token] = user.remember_token
  end
 ・・・
end
```

`cookies`は`session`と使用方法は同じ。

`permanent`でクッキーの有効期限を自動で設定している。

ユーザーのIDをそのままクッキーに保存するのはあまりよくないから`signed`を使って保存前に暗号化している。

- ログインしてユーザーを保持する（`app/controllers/sessions_controller.rb`）

```
class SessionsController < ApplicationController
 ・・・
  def create
    user = User.find_by(email: params[:session][:email].downcase)
    if user && user.authenticate(params[:session][:password])
      log_in user
      remember user
      redirect_to user
    else
      flash.now[:danger] = 'Invalid email/password combination'
      render 'new'
    end
  end
 ・・・
end
```

`app/helpers/sessions_helper.rb`で作成した`remember`メソッドを使用。

- 永続的セッションのcurrent_userを更新（`app/helpers/sessions_helper.rb`）

```
module SessionsHelper
  ・・・
  def current_user
    if (user_id = session[:user_id])
      @current_user ||= User.find_by(id: user_id)
    elsif (user_id = cookies.signed[:user_id])
      user = User.find_by(id: user_id)
      if user && user.authenticated?(cookies[:remember_token])
        log_in user
        @current_user = user
      end
    end
  end
 ・・・
end
```

条件式で定義した`user_id`にセッションまたはクッキーのユーザーIDを与えて判定している。

※ この時点ではクッキーを削除する手段がないからテストは失敗する（`RED`）。

author: gandalf2k15
body:
## About The Pull Request

Alright so this was a bounty request from Grunnyyy, and it makes sense for our server. 

This adds a system for examining things that we want to be meta protected. For now it is only the system for doing it + 1 example. I may return to this and update all uplink items to use the system for special descs.

The way it works is by checking a few conditions depending on the special_desc_req and will display custom extra examine information. 

When reworking an item, make sure to set the standard desc to something normal and the name too! Then set the special_desc_reqs to what you want, and then set the special_desc to the syndicate/whatever description. It's a bit of manual labour but will be worth it for our upcoming antag rework.

It can be expanded as time goes on, I may incorporate an upgraded security hud to bypass the syndicate checks.

## Current settings
```
EXAMINE_CHECK_NONE		//Displays the special_desc regardless if it's set.
EXAMINE_CHECK_SYNDICATE 		//For displaying descriptors for those with the SYNDICATE faction assigned.
EXAMINE_CHECK_SYNDICATE_TOY  //Ditto, only instead of displaying nothing for heathens, it shows "The src looks like a toy, not the real thing."
EXAMINE_CHECK_MINDSHIELD	//For displaying descriptors for those with a mindshield implant.
EXAMINE_CHECK_ROLE	//For displaying description information based on a specific ROLE, e.g. traitor. Remember to set the special_desc_role var on the item.
EXAMINE_CHECK_JOB	//For displaying descriptors for specific jobs, e.g scientist. Remember to set the special_desc_job var on the item.
EXAMINE_CHECK_FACTION		//For displaying descriptors for mob factions, e.g. a zombie, or... turrets. Or syndicate. Remember to set special_desc_factions.
```

Setting an item up correctly, here's an example:
```
/obj/item/storage/backpack/duffelbag/syndie
	name = "duffel bag"
	desc = "A large duffel bag for holding extra supplies."
	special_desc_requirement = EXAMINE_CHECK_SYNDICATE
	special_desc = "This bag is used to store tactical equipment and is manufactured by the syndicate."
```

This results in (if you are a traitor or other syndicate role):
![image](https://i.imgur.com/twlnGYr.png)

## The detective!
This makes the detective fuckin' useful as hell! They're able to see the descriptions because of their brilliant detective skills.
This is what THEY see:
![image](https://i.imgur.com/RgGMwx7.png)


## Changelog
:cl:
add: Added a new in-depth examine system that will be used for future antag reworks.
/:cl:

body:
This PR updates [pip](https://pypi.org/project/pip) from **19.1.1** to **21.0.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 21.0.1
   ```
   ===================

Bug Fixes
---------

- commands: debug: Use packaging.version.parse to compare between versions. (`9461 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9461>`_)
- New resolver: Download and prepare a distribution only at the last possible
  moment to avoid unnecessary network access when the same version is already
  installed locally. (`9516 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9516>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade packaging to 20.9
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.0
   ```
   =================

Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- Drop support for Python 2. (`6148 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6148>`_)
- Remove support for legacy wheel cache entries that were created with pip
  versions older than 20.0. (`7502 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7502>`_)
- Remove support for VCS pseudo URLs editable requirements. It was emitting
  deprecation warning since version 20.0. (`7554 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7554>`_)
- Modernise the codebase after Python 2. (`8802 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8802>`_)
- Drop support for Python 3.5. (`9189 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9189>`_)
- Remove the VCS export feature that was used only with editable VCS
  requirements and had correctness issues. (`9338 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9338>`_)

Features
--------

- Add ``--ignore-requires-python`` support to pip download. (`1884 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/1884>`_)
- New resolver: Error message shown when a wheel contains inconsistent metadata
  is made more helpful by including both values from the file name and internal
  metadata. (`9186 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9186>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- Fix a regression that made ``pip wheel`` do a VCS export instead of a VCS clone
  for editable requirements. This broke VCS requirements that need the VCS
  information to build correctly. (`9273 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9273>`_)
- Fix ``pip download`` of editable VCS requirements that need VCS information
  to build correctly. (`9337 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9337>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade msgpack to 1.0.2.
- Upgrade requests to 2.25.1.

Improved Documentation
----------------------

- Render the unreleased pip version change notes on the news page in docs. (`9172 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9172>`_)
- Fix broken email link in docs feedback banners. (`9343 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9343>`_)


.. note

    You should *NOT* be adding new change log entries to this file, this
    file is managed by towncrier. You *may* edit previous change logs to
    fix problems like typo corrections or such.

    To add a new change log entry, please see
        https://pip.pypa.io/en/latest/development/contributing/#news-entries

.. towncrier release notes start
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.4
   ```
   ===================

Features
--------

- ``pip wheel`` now verifies the built wheel contains valid metadata, and can be
  installed by a subsequent ``pip install``. This can be disabled with
  ``--no-verify``. (`9206 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9206>`_)
- Improve presentation of XMLRPC errors in pip search. (`9315 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9315>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- Fixed hanging VCS subprocess calls when the VCS outputs a large amount of data
  on stderr. Restored logging of VCS errors that was inadvertently removed in pip
  20.2. (`8876 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8876>`_)
- Fix error when an existing incompatibility is unable to be applied to a backtracked state. (`9180 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9180>`_)
- New resolver: Discard a faulty distribution, instead of quitting outright.
  This implementation is taken from 20.2.2, with a fix that always makes the
  resolver iterate through candidates from indexes lazily, to avoid downloading
  candidates we do not need. (`9203 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9203>`_)
- New resolver: Discard a source distribution if it fails to generate metadata,
  instead of quitting outright. This implementation is taken from 20.2.2, with a
  fix that always makes the resolver iterate through candidates from indexes
  lazily, to avoid downloading candidates we do not need. (`9246 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9246>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade resolvelib to 0.5.4.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.3
   ```
   ===================

Bug Fixes
---------

- Revert "Skip candidate not providing valid metadata", as that caused pip to be overeager about downloading from the package index. (`9264 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9264>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.2
   ```
   ===================

Features
--------

- New resolver: Resolve direct and pinned (``==`` or ``===``) requirements first
  to improve resolver performance. (`9185 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9185>`_)
- Add a mechanism to delay resolving certain packages, and use it for setuptools. (`9249 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9249>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- New resolver: The "Requirement already satisfied" log is not printed only once
  for each package during resolution. (`9117 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9117>`_)
- Fix crash when logic for redacting authentication information from URLs
  in ``--help`` is given a list of strings, instead of a single string. (`9191 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9191>`_)
- New resolver: Correctly implement PEP 592. Do not return yanked versions from
  an index, unless the version range can only be satisfied by yanked candidates. (`9203 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9203>`_)
- New resolver: Make constraints also apply to package variants with extras, so
  the resolver correctly avoids backtracking on them. (`9232 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9232>`_)
- New resolver: Discard a candidate if it fails to provide metadata from source,
  or if the provided metadata is inconsistent, instead of quitting outright. (`9246 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9246>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Update vendoring to 20.8

Improved Documentation
----------------------

- Update documentation to reflect that pip still uses legacy resolver by default in Python 2 environments. (`9269 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9269>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.1
   ```
   ===================

Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- The --build-dir option has been restored as a no-op, to soften the transition
  for tools that still used it. (`9193 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9193>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3
   ```
   - Introduce a new ResolutionImpossible error, raised when pip encounters un-satisfiable dependency conflicts (`8546 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8546>`_, `#8377 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8377>`_)
- Add a subcommand ``debug`` to ``pip config`` to list available configuration sources and the key-value pairs defined in them. (`6741 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6741>`_)
- Warn if index pages have unexpected content-type (`6754 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6754>`_)
- Allow specifying ``--prefer-binary`` option in a requirements file (`7693 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7693>`_)
- Generate PEP 376 REQUESTED metadata for user supplied requirements installed
  by pip. (`7811 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7811>`_)
- Warn if package url is a vcs or an archive url with invalid scheme (`8128 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8128>`_)
- Parallelize network operations in ``pip list``. (`8504 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8504>`_)

This fix will require a clone of the original base URL which can then be joined to the value in the `LOCATION` header if it is a relative path. Previously this would simply return an Error for RelativeURLWithoutBase.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pip](https://pypi.org/project/pip) from **20.2.2** to **21.0.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 21.0.1
   ```
   ===================

Bug Fixes
---------

- commands: debug: Use packaging.version.parse to compare between versions. (`9461 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9461>`_)
- New resolver: Download and prepare a distribution only at the last possible
  moment to avoid unnecessary network access when the same version is already
  installed locally. (`9516 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9516>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade packaging to 20.9
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.0
   ```
   =================

Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- Drop support for Python 2. (`6148 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6148>`_)
- Remove support for legacy wheel cache entries that were created with pip
  versions older than 20.0. (`7502 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7502>`_)
- Remove support for VCS pseudo URLs editable requirements. It was emitting
  deprecation warning since version 20.0. (`7554 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7554>`_)
- Modernise the codebase after Python 2. (`8802 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8802>`_)
- Drop support for Python 3.5. (`9189 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9189>`_)
- Remove the VCS export feature that was used only with editable VCS
  requirements and had correctness issues. (`9338 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9338>`_)

Features
--------

- Add ``--ignore-requires-python`` support to pip download. (`1884 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/1884>`_)
- New resolver: Error message shown when a wheel contains inconsistent metadata
  is made more helpful by including both values from the file name and internal
  metadata. (`9186 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9186>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- Fix a regression that made ``pip wheel`` do a VCS export instead of a VCS clone
  for editable requirements. This broke VCS requirements that need the VCS
  information to build correctly. (`9273 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9273>`_)
- Fix ``pip download`` of editable VCS requirements that need VCS information
  to build correctly. (`9337 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9337>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade msgpack to 1.0.2.
- Upgrade requests to 2.25.1.

Improved Documentation
----------------------

- Render the unreleased pip version change notes on the news page in docs. (`9172 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9172>`_)
- Fix broken email link in docs feedback banners. (`9343 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9343>`_)


.. note

    You should *NOT* be adding new change log entries to this file, this
    file is managed by towncrier. You *may* edit previous change logs to
    fix problems like typo corrections or such.

    To add a new change log entry, please see
        https://pip.pypa.io/en/latest/development/contributing/#news-entries

.. towncrier release notes start
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.4
   ```
   ===================

Features
--------

- ``pip wheel`` now verifies the built wheel contains valid metadata, and can be
  installed by a subsequent ``pip install``. This can be disabled with
  ``--no-verify``. (`9206 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9206>`_)
- Improve presentation of XMLRPC errors in pip search. (`9315 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9315>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- Fixed hanging VCS subprocess calls when the VCS outputs a large amount of data
  on stderr. Restored logging of VCS errors that was inadvertently removed in pip
  20.2. (`8876 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8876>`_)
- Fix error when an existing incompatibility is unable to be applied to a backtracked state. (`9180 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9180>`_)
- New resolver: Discard a faulty distribution, instead of quitting outright.
  This implementation is taken from 20.2.2, with a fix that always makes the
  resolver iterate through candidates from indexes lazily, to avoid downloading
  candidates we do not need. (`9203 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9203>`_)
- New resolver: Discard a source distribution if it fails to generate metadata,
  instead of quitting outright. This implementation is taken from 20.2.2, with a
  fix that always makes the resolver iterate through candidates from indexes
  lazily, to avoid downloading candidates we do not need. (`9246 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9246>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Upgrade resolvelib to 0.5.4.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.3
   ```
   ===================

Bug Fixes
---------

- Revert "Skip candidate not providing valid metadata", as that caused pip to be overeager about downloading from the package index. (`9264 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9264>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.2
   ```
   ===================

Features
--------

- New resolver: Resolve direct and pinned (``==`` or ``===``) requirements first
  to improve resolver performance. (`9185 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9185>`_)
- Add a mechanism to delay resolving certain packages, and use it for setuptools. (`9249 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9249>`_)

Bug Fixes
---------

- New resolver: The "Requirement already satisfied" log is not printed only once
  for each package during resolution. (`9117 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9117>`_)
- Fix crash when logic for redacting authentication information from URLs
  in ``--help`` is given a list of strings, instead of a single string. (`9191 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9191>`_)
- New resolver: Correctly implement PEP 592. Do not return yanked versions from
  an index, unless the version range can only be satisfied by yanked candidates. (`9203 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9203>`_)
- New resolver: Make constraints also apply to package variants with extras, so
  the resolver correctly avoids backtracking on them. (`9232 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9232>`_)
- New resolver: Discard a candidate if it fails to provide metadata from source,
  or if the provided metadata is inconsistent, instead of quitting outright. (`9246 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9246>`_)

Vendored Libraries
------------------

- Update vendoring to 20.8

Improved Documentation
----------------------

- Update documentation to reflect that pip still uses legacy resolver by default in Python 2 environments. (`9269 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9269>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3.1
   ```
   ===================

Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- The --build-dir option has been restored as a no-op, to soften the transition
  for tools that still used it. (`9193 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9193>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.3
   ```
   - Introduce a new ResolutionImpossible error, raised when pip encounters un-satisfiable dependency conflicts (`8546 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8546>`_, `#8377 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8377>`_)
- Add a subcommand ``debug`` to ``pip config`` to list available configuration sources and the key-value pairs defined in them. (`6741 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6741>`_)
- Warn if index pages have unexpected content-type (`6754 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6754>`_)
- Allow specifying ``--prefer-binary`` option in a requirements file (`7693 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7693>`_)
- Generate PEP 376 REQUESTED metadata for user supplied requirements installed
  by pip. (`7811 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7811>`_)
- Warn if package url is a vcs or an archive url with invalid scheme (`8128 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8128>`_)
- Parallelize network operations in ``pip list``. (`8504 <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8504>`_)

This PR updates [jsonpickle](https://pypi.org/project/jsonpickle) from **1.1** to **1.5.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 1.5.1
   ```
   ======
    * The performance of the unpickler was drastically improved by
      avoiding tag checks for basic Python types.  (+340)
    * ``decode()`` documentation improvements.  (+341)
    * Serialization of Pandas DataFrame objects that contain
      timedelta64[ns] dtypes are now supported.  (+330) (331)
    * Dictionary identity is now preserved.  For example, if the same
      dictionary appears twice in a list, the reconstituted list
      will now contain two references to the same dictionary.  (255) (+332)
    * Unit tests were added to ensure that sklearn.tree.DecisionTreeClassifier
      objects are properly serialized.  (155) (+344)
    * The ``is_reducible()`` utility function used by ``encode()`` is now
      4x faster!  Objects that provide ``__getstate__()``, ``__setstate__()``,
      and ``__slots__`` benefit most from these improvements.  (+343)
    * Improved pickler ``flatten()/encode()`` performance.  (+345)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.5.0
   ```
   ======
    * Previous versions of jsonpickle with `make_refs=False` would emit
      ``null`` when encountering an object it had already seen when
      traversing objects.  All instances of the object are now serialized.
      While this is arguably an improvement in the vast majority of
      scenarios, it is a change in behavior and is thus considered a
      minor-level change.  (333) (334) (337) (+338)
    * Multiple enums are now serialized correctly with `make_refs=False`.  (235)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.4.2
   ```
   ======
    * Use importlib.metadata from the stdlib on Python 3.8.  (+305) (303)
    * Micro-optimize type checks to use a `set` for lookups. (+327)
    * Documentation improvements.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.4.1
   ```
   ======
    * Patch release for Python 3.8 `importlib_metadata` support.
      (300)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.4
   ```
   ====
    * Python 3.8 support.  (292)
    * ``jsonpickle.encode`` now supports the standard ``indent``
      and ``separators`` arguments, and passes them through to the
      active JSON backend library.  (183)
    * We now include a custom handler for `array.array` objects.  (199)
    * Dict key order is preserved when pickling dictionaries on Python3.  (193)
    * Improved serialization of dictionaries with non-string keys.
      Previously, using an enum that was both the key and a value in
      a dictionary could end up with incorrect references to other
      objects.  The references are now properly maintained for dicts
      with object keys that are also referenced in the dict's values.  (286)
    * Improved serialization of pandas.Series objects.  (287)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.3
   ```
   ====
    * Improved round tripping of default dicts.  (+283) (282)

    * Better support for cyclical references when encoding with
      ``unpicklable=False``.  (+264)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.2
   ```
   ====
    * Simplified JSON representation for `__reduce__` values.  (+261)

    * Improved Pandas support with new handlers for more Pandas data types.
      (+256)

    * Prevent stack overflows caused by bugs in user-defined `__getstate__`
      functions which cause infinite recursion.  (+260)
      (259)

    * Improved support for objects that contain dicts with Integer keys.
      Previously, jsonpickle could not restore objects that contained
      dicts with integer keys and provided getstate only.
      These objects are now handled robustly.  (247).

    * Support for encoding binary data in `base85`_ instead of base64 has been
      added on Python 3. Base85 produces payloads about 10% smaller than base64,
      albeit at the cost of lower throughput.  For performance and backwards
      compatibility with Python 2 the pickler uses base64 by default, but it can
      be configured to use ``base85`` with the new ``use_base85`` argument.
      (251).

    * Dynamic SQLAlchemy tables in SQLAlchemy >= 1.3 are now supported.
      (254).

.. _base85: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascii85

author: iamdtang
body:
## 1. The Procfile

Create a `Procfile` in the root of your Laravel project. See the "Files changed" tab in this pull request for what to put in that file.

## 2. Environment Variables

Create environment variables for the following variables in your `.env` file. To get to the environment variables page on the Heroku site, go to the `Settings` tab of your application and click on the `Reveal Config Vars` button.

```
DB_CONNECTION=
DB_HOST=
DB_PORT=
DB_DATABASE=
DB_USERNAME=
DB_PASSWORD=
APP_DEBUG=true
APP_KEY=
```

Normally we wouldn't set `APP_DEBUG` to `true` in a production application. 

For the purposes of this class, using your local development `APP_KEY` is fine.

## 3. Fixing route generation issues

Currently, the `route()` function generates URLs with `http` instead of `https` on Heroku. This presents a problem for POST routes, like when submitting a form, as you'll likely see the "419 | Page Expired" page. To fix this, add the following to `routes/web.php`, similar to [this commit](https://github.com/ITP-405-Spring-2021/music-app/commit/83ee4c87cfea7a8540c3b345096457b7aa8e2adf):

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\URL;

if (env('APP_ENV') !== 'local') {
    URL::forceScheme('https');
}
```

## Optional

The `APP_KEY` is used primarily for encrypting cookies. As described on the blog post [`APP_KEY` and You](https://tighten.co/blog/app-key-and-you/):

> Once your app is running, there's one place it uses the APP_KEY: cookies. Laravel uses the key for all encrypted cookies, including the session cookie, before handing them off to the user's browser, and it uses it to decrypt cookies read from the browser. This prevents the client from making changes to their cookies and granting themselves admin privileges or impersonating another user in your application. Encrypted cookies are an important security feature in Laravel.

If you don't want to use your development `APP_KEY`, [install the Heroku CLI](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-cli).

Next, run the following __for your Heroku app name (which isn't itp-405)__:

1. `heroku run bash --app=itp-405`. Be sure to replace __itp-405__ with your Heroku app name.
2. `php artisan key:generate --show`
3. Copy the key
4. `exit`
5. `heroku config:set APP_KEY=PASTE THE KEY YOU JUST COPIED HERE --app=itp-405`. Be sure to replace __itp-405__ with your Heroku app name.

Here is my deployed app: https://itp-405.herokuapp.com/invoices

body:
Hi @jherr ,

I made a fork and tested this on my forked version.
I can successfully build & deploy to Github pages and access it.
The changes should work on the original repo without any further steps.
https://pazel-io.github.io/jmusic/

The only manual step is to create an ssh key and then:
1.  Add the public key of that ssh key to **Deploy keys** under the settings of `jherr/jmusic`.
2. Add the secret key of that ssh key to **Secrets** under the settings of `jherr/jmusic` with the name **ACTIONS_DEPLOY_KEY**. (this name is used in the deploy script, so it should match)

author: mikestead
body:
Adding support for budget thresholds for primary metrics. 

```console
lighthouse-batch -s https://web.dev \
    --score 92 \
    --seo 95 \
    --pwa 85 \
    --best-practices 90 \
    --accessibility 100 \
    --fail-fast
```

The `--fail-fast` option will error as soon as a budget is exceeded and skip pending sites. Otherwise any and all budget errors will be printed once all sites have run, before exiting with code 1.

Fixes #29

author: sethaxen
body:
~Fixes the sign of blocks for half-integral degrees. Not strictly necessary because we don't use half-integral blocks, but nice to know the general version works.~

Edit: Technically the half-integral blocks are representations of SU(2), not SO(3), so they follow a different composition rule. Informally, SU(2) is a sphere, and SO(3) is one of its hemispheres. If we embed SO(3) in SU(2), then composition of two rotations in SO(3) can produce a rotation in SU(2). However, if we don't embed it, then the resulting rotation will be in SO(3). Constructing a half-integral block implicitly maps to SU(2) first, hence a different composition rule is followed. Again, we don't use the half-integral blocks anyways, so this isn't a problem, but it's good to know that the test suite picked up on this.

body:
Overflow caused by using int32_t instead of int64_t

vrolandAPP 6:02 PM
Nice catch, that's a classic overflow right here! esp_timer_get_time() returns an int64_t, but t_poweron is uint32_t. So, after 2^32/10^6/60 = 71.5 min = 1 hour 11 minutes t_poweron overflows and time_since_poweron_m will be > 10. Changing the time of t_poweron to int64_t should fix it :)

author: suyjuris
body:
# Summary
Factorio silently accepts an out-of-bounds insertion index in table.insert, but [YAFC](https://github.com/ShadowTheAge/yafc), in particular, does not, causing a crash.

# Steps to Reproduce
I unpacked a fresh Factorio 1.1.19 and installed SeaBlock 0.5.2 (which pulls in angelsbioprocessing_0.7.17, angelspetrochem_0.9.17, angelsrefining, angelsrefining_0.11.19, angelssmelting_0.6.14, A Sea Block Config_0.5.1, bobelectronics_1.1.3, boblibrary_1.1.2, boblogistics_1.1.2, bobplates_1.1.2). Then I installed the upstream version of YAFC (commit 72dd2810, version 0.5.4.1) and pointed it towards the aforementioned Factorio install:

```
Unhandled exception. YAFC.Parser.LuaException: (SeaBlock, lib.lua):42: bad argument #2 to 'insert' (position out of bounds)
stack traceback:
[C]: in ?
[C]: in function 'insert'
(SeaBlock, lib.lua):42: in function 'moveeffect'
(SeaBlock, data-updates/startup.lua):301: in main chunk
[C]: in function 'require'
(SeaBlock, data-updates.lua):14: in main chunk
```

# Details

The lines in the above stacktrace try to perform a `table.insert` with an out-of-bounds insertion index. Factorio accepts this silently, creating a malformed list (i.e. `table.insert({1, 1}, 2, 30)` results in `{1, 1, [30] = 2}`), but the lua runtime used by YAFC complains.

Of course, out-of-bounds inserts ideally should not happen at all, then this would not be a problem, but for the moment the attached commit should make the behaviour consistent and less brittle.

author: 1c3t3a
body:
During development I've often came across problems related to async rust. When I started the project I thought it would be a nice thing to have the whole crate use rusts async API, but now it just feels like it decreases the development speed. As this is mostly a learning project for me, I think it might be a good idea to refactor the code to be normal, sync rust. We might switch back to async later, when the whole protocol is implemented and the API is fix.

Changes in this PR:

- Removed all async code (originated from the async HTTP requests made via reqwest).
- Changed the callback functions of the socket.io client from `Fn` to `FnMut`, because this allows using the socket within the callback.

author: bigopon
body:
# Pull Request ## 📖 Description This PR brings a new capability to content interpolation, so that it treats both primtive values (non object values, and array), and HTML nodes equally. That means that if a dynamic part of a content interpolation yields a HTML node or element, it should be inserted into its location as is, rather than first converted to string. ## Current state Currently, interpolation binding is done via following form: ```html
You have ${count} items
``` And if the bound view model has `count` value equal 10, the html should be equal to `
You have 10 items
`. This works for most scenarios. Now let's say if we want to have the HTML a bit differently: the number should be red when `count` value is 0, and green otherwise. At the moment, there' three ways to do it: 1. Use some extra markup and apply dynamic styling to it: ```html
You have ${count} items
``` 2. turn the above into html binding via: ```html
``` Where `colorise` is a value converter with the follow simplistic implementation for example purpose: ```ts class ColoriseValueConverter { toView(val) { return `${val}`; } } ``` 3. use a custom element with exposed properties to adjust the styling of the text: ```html
You have items
``` #### some cons: For (1): the template is now coupled with some low noise for styling purposes. It's not bad. Though overtime, the application templates could look undesirably complicated. Also, the wrapping element (`span`) is fixed, which means if we want to have font-weight bold for the `count`, we either need to add more markup (``), or styles which could push the complexity further. For (2): having to use `innerhtml` is not always desirable, also, it's not natural syntax one would expect doing some text/content interpolation. With both of the above approaches, it's takes some minor to medium effort to refactor the template code. Also, because of this, higher level plugins, such as `validation`, `i18n` has no way but resolve to using `innerHTML` as a way to provide their features. For (3): this is the preferred approach in almost all scenarios, as it's flexible in what inputs it can accept, and powerful in what output it can produce (paraphrased what @jods4 comment on this). This also produces no fragmentation in the framework as there's no difference between interpolation in a normal text, and in an attribute. Though, there's an edge that this feature (interpolation with HTML nodes) has over custom element: stronger script-based templating for where flexibility, perf really matters. ## Feature The interpolation binding & renderer could be enhanced, so that they understand & allow HTML nodes as primitive parts without converting them to a string for final DOM result. For the example above, we can keep the original template, with slight modification from `${count}` to `${count | colorise}` ```html
You have ${count | colorise} items
``` and change the `colorise` value converter implementation to: ```ts class ColoriseValueConverter { toView(val) { const span = document.createElement('span'); span.textContent = val; span.styles.color = val === 0 ? 'red' : green; return span; // note that this is an actual html element } } ``` And the final, rendered html, for `count` equals 0, would be ```html
You have 0 items
``` #### Changes 1. At the moment, whole text interpolation is turned into a single text node, and the final string is computed from all parts, then concatenated and updated. To support this feature, each static text part should be a text node of its own, and each dynamic part is also a text node, starting empty. This text node is used for both content & "render location" purposes. If the value of a dynamic part is an HTML node, then it will be inserted before this text node. 2. Performance wise: for text interpolation, it's probably worse if there' many dynamic parts in an interpolation whole. As each dynamic parts is now updated independently, instead of collectively updated as a whole like before. 3. Correctness wise: it got better, as individual dynamic part can now be updated in different rate. In a future where we want to allow throttling to-view. ## (Possible) Caveats - HTML nodes (text/element) are appended as is (without cloning), which means if the same value is appended in multiple places, the last use wins. ## 📑 Test Plan - Existing interpolation tests work - Add new tests for interpolation with value converters that return html nodes - Add new tests for the caveat of the same html node being appended in multiple places ## ⏭ Next Steps - Investigate some `i18n` implementation that can benefit from this change - Promote the use of computed html content & interpolation, for web component content composition. An immediate integration target we can have is FAST, `hyperhtml`, `lit-html` html renderer. Consider the following example: ```ts class MyApp { gridColumns = [ { name: 'name', heading: (rows, column) => html`
...
`, cell: data => html`
${data.name}
` }, { name: 'value', heading: (rows, column) => html`
...
`, cell: data => html`
${data.value}
` }, ] } ``` and template: ```html grid.html
${col.heading(rowDatas, col)}
${col.cell(rowData)}
``` - Not determined: Ability to append multiple html nodes? as this support for `DocumentFragment` won't be easy (needs a way to keep track of its node) ## Acknowledgement This feature takes the inspiration from the work of content interpolation done in [MS FAST](https://www.fast.design/)

Fix string operator `$|` (aka string-contains) which was not detecting a pattern at the start of the string

```
on var1#state do if (%value%=TEST) publish debug/equal %value% endif endon
on var1#state do if (%value%$|TEST) publish debug/contains %value% endif endon
on var1#state do if (%value%$<TEST) publish debug/startwith %value% endif endon
on var1#state do if (%value%$>TEST) publish debug/endwith %value% endif endon
on var1#state do if (%value%$!TEST) publish debug/notequal %value% endif endon
on var1#state do if (%value%$^TEST) publish debug/notcontains %value% endif endon

on var1#state$|TEST do publish debug/contains %value% endon

on var1#state$!TEST do publish debug/notequal %value% endon

author: pajlada
body:
There were two ways to create a SwitchSplitItem:
a) A Container only: This would let the user switch to a Tab only, but not change which split in the focus was focused
b) A split only: This would programmatically fill in the container (by querying the split) and let the user switch to the Tab and change focus to the split

Since split had no way to programmatically get its container, we can
instead require that the container is always filled in. Where this class
is used (QuickSwitcherPopup.cpp:97 and QuickSwitcherPopup:108) we do
have the container pointer already, so the logic for creating a
SwitchSplitItem has now changed to:
a) A container but no split
b) A container and a split

author: dreamwhite
body:
Fixed Booter/Quirks according to OpenCore Configuration.pdf.

In order to determine whether `ProvideCustomSlide` must be enabled (so paired with `EnableSafeModeSlide`) or not, edit the EFI as it follows:

- Use OpenCore DEBUG binaries
- `config.plist/Misc/Debug/Target` set to `67` (so it logs everything in a txt file)

Then boot, and check the txt file by looking for `All slides are usable! You can disable ProvideCustomSlide`.
If you find a match, then disable:

- `config.plist/Booter/Quirks/EnableSafeModeSlide`
- `config.plist/Booter/Quirks/ProvideCustomSlide`

Else, leave them untouched.
Finally restore the OpenCore binaries and set `config.plist/Misc/Debug/Target` set to `3`.

author: 2asoft
body:
- Downgrade to a slightly older emscripten version 2.0.9
2.0.10 made a change that causes `dynCall` to no longer be defined, which breaks the emscripten glue code for this project.
Fixing this would probably involve building an isolated repro and possibly getting a fix into emscripten codebase.
I am not an emscripten expert and I dont understand what exactly happens and why, so downgrading to a recent working version instead.

- Don't SDL_Quit in the web version
Emscripten has its own idea of how the main loop should be invoked.
This results in `cmain` returning early.
This is fine, because code continues to run and no resources are actually torn down by exiting from `cmain`.
Calling SDL_Quit after `cmain` means that is no longer true; GL context, and all the other SDL structures, are gone too soon.

- Don't force Windows kernel v5 in web version
This was done previously to fix a rendering bug in Linux by ensuring unlocked DX surfaces are always used (not fully sure how this translates to SDL).
However, the web requires the opposite of this behaviour.
This change simply narrows down the Linux specific fix to non-emscripten builds.
A proper fix would be understanding of the surface-locking stuff and possibly separate renderers and/or something that determines capabilities of each platform. Not today :)

author: nasf-fan
body:
The pre-detect uncommitted DTX during vos iteration is some
kind optimization for try to reduce the RPC overhead caused
by related DTX refresh. But the optimization may cause some
issues as following:

1. It cannot handle non-committed DTX when vos_iter_probe().
   That is the first place to detect non-committed DTX entry
   that may affect current iteration. If we skip over it, we
   may skip related tree under such point. That may make the
   pre-detection of uncommitted DTX to become meaningless or
   cause more overhead.

2. Similarly for non-committed DTX when handle vos_iter_next.

3. Need to consider CPU yield during the pre-detection scan.
   For the object with a lot of keys/values, hundreds of or
   thousands of pre-detection may not find more uncommitted
   DTX but introduce more overhead. But if we do not do CPU
   yield during that, other ULTs may be starve.

So before we have enough verification for the effectiveness,
we will restore the original vos iteration logic before the
optimization.

On the other hand, the patch also resolves the issue of DTX
handle mess-up caused by the vos iteration CPU yield: every
iteration stores its DTX handle in vos_iterator::it_dth when
prepare the iteration, then in subsequent prober/fetch/next,
the iteration can set DTX handle on TLS when need and reset
(as original value) after using immediately. CPU yield for
iteration only happens during pre_cb or post_cb callback,
the DTX handle on TLS has already been restored at that time.

Signed-off-by: Fan Yong <fan.yong@intel.com>

author: nerrad
body:
As a companion to a proposal for starting to use TypeScript in the blocks repo, I've created this pull request. I'm not going to go into the benefits and why we'd want to switch to TS in this pr description (that's for our internal deliberation) however, they are many. One significant thing I already noticed while working on the initial conversion was some minor bugs surfaced as the types were implemented (mostly around not accounting for possible new properties in the Cart API response and some guards around unknown data shapes in the reducer).

Since TypeScript is a fairly trivial enhancement on top of native JS, it's not too difficult to pick up the syntax and should be relatively easy to adopt. 

Some notes about what's introduced in this PR:

- I reviewed a number of WordPress project configs using TS (including Calypso and other projects) and the config I landed on is one that I _think_ will be okay for Blocks. But I'm not an expert here so this is open for modification.
- I stuck with babel-loader for typescript transpilation because that allows us to more easily keep many of the other babel plugins we have in use (along with inheriting @wordpress/* babel configs). AFAICT, this is sufficient, the only caveat is that there won't be any hard ts-loader breaks on type errors during builds. I think this is sufficiently covered by the additional linting put in place however.
- Some new `@types/*` packages were installed for various types being used. 
- There's some typing I implemented that I had trouble with so I just applied `@ts-ignore` to those places for now. As we get more proficient with TS (or others more skilled take a look at the code) we can address.
- We don't have to convert everything over to TypeScript immediately - our existing code can live with the ts files indefinitely. But it is something we'll probably want to chip away at (and/or implement with new code) if we decide to go all in. The benefits will only be fully realized as we type more of our code.
- I'm finding that I really prefer full TS over the jsdoc flavored TS we were using as it's more expressive and less finagling with how to setup typedefs etc.

Some things we may want to consider:

- The benefit of `@param` and `@return` jsdocs is less useful in TypeScript files because it's kind of redundant with the existing typing. I wonder if we should remove those jsdoc rulesets for TS files (and just accept jsdoc descriptions where needed)?
- There may be other eslint rules we can relax/remove in TS files because of the gains with typing - we should watch for them.

## To Test

Anything interacting with the Cart data store will need to be tested because of some minor changes done in the PR. This pretty much means anything with the All Products block and the Cart and Checkout blocks. So full flow tests should be done. However, any problems that exist should surface immediately because of the low level impact of the changes.

## Next steps

- Decide if we want to go all in with TS
- Merge this pull and establish some guidelines for new work being written in TS.
- Slowly chip away at migrating existing code to TS (I would start with anything that is at the base level and then work down the tree - so data stores, base components/hooks/context, and then blocks).

Building from the work by @tudi2d  in #1074, update methods:

author: peterhillman
body:
Address https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=30115

OpenEXR images were always supposed to have at least one channel. This change adds the missing sanity check to prevent reading or writing files with no channel list, or with an empty channel list.

It is theoretically possible to create a file with an empty channel list, but it will always be flagged as incomplete.
Since such files are non-standard and unexpected, software reading such files may misbehave in ways that could be exploited.
For safety, it seems safer to add the explicit check to prevent handling such files.

For future-proofing, this test only runs on known types. In the future a new OpenEXR library may add a new 'part type' that does not contain a channel list attribute. Files with such parts would pass this sanity check so they could be (partially) loaded by existing versions of the library.

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

Right now, the Kafka Connect build starts a new build in every reconciliation. Even if the previous one for example took just too long time and timed out the original reconciliation. author: pvid
body:
Hi! Thank you for all the work on gradle <-> scalafix integration!

This PR is a draft of a solution to https://github.com/cosmicsilence/gradle-scalafix/issues/32 https://github.com/cosmicsilence/gradle-scalafix/issues/19

I have run into issues with using semantic rules with a a 2.13 project 

- `ExplicitResultTypes` rule needs the scala binary version of the project and scalafix to match
- I had a hard time configuring the [liancheng's organize import rule](https://github.com/liancheng/scalafix-organize-imports), because I tried to use the artefact for 2.13. I feel that it leads to non-intuitive situations where you need to use rules compiled for 2.12 because the plugin depends on a 2.12 version of scalafix.

Another issue is that depending on a scala artifact pollutes the build classpath which causes conflicts with other gradle plugins that depend on different binary versions of Scala.

I also changed the version of SemanticDB the plugin autoconfigures - I propose to always use the project's version. I believe that is similar to what [sbt-scalafix](https://github.com/scalacenter/sbt-scalafix/blob/402c2433aa9369b8c0c1c27fedc1fe4504f6bd8f/src/main/scala/scalafix/sbt/ScalafixPlugin.scala#L95) does. If a required version of the SemanticDB is not would, it will result in a resolution error instead of a warning (which is the current behaviour)

This is my first time writing groovy and contributing to a Gradle plugins. Any feedback would be much appreciated. I'd be happy to amend the PR or scrap it all together if you'd want to go another way

author: hishamhm
body:
This is an MVP for dumping type information for consumption by third-party tools.

These were my high-level goals:

* minimal tl API
* not exposing the raw AST
* simple output, designed for quick lookup
* JSON output in the CLI

Right now the main thing is a map mapping filename:y:x positions to types.

One next improvement to add would be mapping variables to their definition locations (right now they map to their types only).

By visual inspection alone, I have already noticed that some of the information returned is a bit wonky and can be improved (some nested AST nodes report the same x, y positions and I just picked the first one; so we probably should tweak the AST a bit to ensure the most relevant information is returned). But I think this is a good start, and should be a good kickstart for getting feedback on what data is missing and what can work better!

(Visualizing the raw data this way has already prompted some other improvements in the compiler, even, see the other commits in this PR!)

author: andycb
body:
Fixes #34 

Currently the whole time the app is connected to a printer, it attempts to connect to the camera printer every 5 seconds to establish if the printer has a camera and it is enabled. While viewing the camera feed it uses an `img` tag to show the mjpeg stream, while _also_ checking the state every five seconds.

This has caused a couple of issues:
- Chromium has issues when using `img` elements with mjpeg streams - preventing the stream from connecting correctly when the page is navigated away from (#30)
- If the app is left running fir multiple hours, eventually the printer gets slower and the app starts timing out (#34)

The first issue was previously mitigated by calling `window.stop()` on navigate away, but it was a bit of a hack. To fix this more concretely and address the issue of pining the printer too many times this change updates the way the camera works.

When the printer is connected to the app attempt to connect to the camera feed - once connected the app will remain connected for the entire session. If the camera stops sending data the app will trigger a disconnection error.

When viewing the feed, the app will use the data from that connection - meaning that there is only ever one connection to the camera and Chromium never has to deal with mjpeg streams.

author: layoutd
body:
### Changes proposed in this Pull Request:

Adds the essentials of Merchant Center account linking/sub-account creation process. It builds on #179 and modifies the `POST /mc/gla/accounts` endpoint to attempt the following steps in succession:
1. Sub-account creation (using the MCA account). 
   - If an ID is provided, this step is marked as done.
   - A `from_mca` property is added to the option for this step to track what kind of account the user has. This mirrors `gla_merchant_id_mca` right now, which could be removed.
2. Account linking * (TBC).
    - This is likely a two-step process of the MCA requesting access, and the account approving access. It's unclear whether it will be necessary for both types of accounts.
3. Site verification (using the client Google account)

The account linking/sub-account creation process returns two values (or an error if something goes wrong):
    1. The ID of the new sub-account, or the linked account.
    2. The `claim_delay`- the number of seconds to wait before attempting a `claimwebsite` call (generally ~60s in testing so far). It's unclear whether this delay is forced, or if it's a matter of data propagation. In the MC panel, site verification and claim can be done in quick succession.

The `POST /mc/gla/accounts/claimwebsite` endpoint is also added:
1. Site claiming.
   - Can only be attempted once the first three steps have been completed. 
    - Depending on the `from_mca` value, this could be done using the WCS manager (MCA+account) or the WCS proxy (account+account).
    - The MC account must have the site configured as its `websiteUrl` in order to be claimed, so this is something that needs to be configured (already done when creating the sub-account) or double-checked (todo for linked accounts).
    - The controller uses the `timestamp` property in the `account_state` option's `verify` step to determine whether the configured delay has passed since verification, and will return a [503 code with a Retry-After header](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After) if more time is needed.

Any failed step stops the process. The four steps (create, link, verify, claim) are each tracked using the `gla_merchant_account_state` option, which allows the process to be restarted if a certain step fails without repeating the previous steps. 

In order to work:
- Needs to be tested with the following PR included: Automattic/woocommerce-connect-server#1698
- The Google Account needs to be connected (for Site Verification proxy request, some website claims, and likely one leg of the Site Linking step).
- The Manager ID needs to be connected (for the MCA-account processes).
- The Google Account can't be the same as the MCA account because sub-account creation will fail.
- The `site_url()` must be a live site (accessible by Google's Site Verification and Website Claim services). There's a new `woocommerce_gla_site_url` filter that allows a value other than the default `site_url()` to be used.
- The host needs to allow 70+ second requests as there's a forced delay between verification and claiming Google API requests. 


Some notes:
- The account linking process for new sub-accounts is still TBD.
- **IMPORTANT** So far in testing, there needs to be a 60s+ delay between Site Verification and Site Claim (otherwise Site Claim fails). Not sure if this is a forced delay, or if it's the time necessary for the Site Verification to be visible to the Merchant Center. Could use third-party confirmation.
- Site Verification - probably don't need the Controller anymore as it won't be accessed client side. (the site verification logic is currently duplicated to the AccountController and needs to find a unified, permanent home).
- There are quite a few steps that could fail, but whose error message is difficult to reach. For example, when trying to create an account, it's possible that the operation fails because the `websiteUrl` is invalid, and the Google API returns this message. However, the WooCommerce Connect Server returns an error of "Response does not contain an account ID". The Create Account method in proxy throws an error with 'Invalid response when creating account', which is also returned by this endpoint. Access to the WCS is required to suss out the actual error.

**Pending**
- When linking an existing MC account, retrieve the details using `accounts.get` and update the `websiteUrl` using `accounts.update` if necessary, before claiming the website.
- Handle failed claims. The WCS currently only returns a generic "claim failed" message - this could be due to a misconfigured `websiteUrl`, not enough time between verify and claim, or because another account has claimed the URL. In the last case, it's possible to override the claim (if they enable it for the MCA), but the WCS will need to notify that this is the case in order to confirm the override with the user (or simply inform that they need to remove the claim from another MC).
- Determine existing claims. [`accounts.get`](https://developers.google.com/shopping-content/reference/rest/v2.1/accounts/get) and [`accounts.list`](https://developers.google.com/shopping-content/reference/rest/v2.1/accounts/list) (for MCAs) can show the `websiteUrl` associated to the MC account (https://merchants.google.com/mc/settings/website in the MC Panel) but doesn't seem to indicate whether the site has claimed the account (verification can be confirmed using the Site Verification API). Knowing whether an account has claimed their website URL could be useful for (a) overriding existing claims and (b) suggesting that the user link an existing MC account that already has the store URL verified and claimed.

### Detailed test instructions:

1.  Use the `Create MC Sub-Account` button in the Connection Test page.
    - The `Site URL` is populated automatically, but MUST BE a live, unclaimed site for verification and claiming. Any site can be used as long as it has the correct meta tag (visible in the `gla_site_verification` option)
    - The `MC ID` field can be used to link an external MC. Note that the Website URL must be configured manually in the [MC Panel](https://merchants.google.com/mc/settings/website) in order for the claim button to work.
    - The Google Account and Manager Account must both be connected (not confirmed before beginning the process, currently)
    - If any step fails, the same button restarts the process from the last unfinished step.
    - To reset/retest, delete the options `gla_merchant_id`, `gla_merchant_id_mca`, `gla_merchant_account_state`, and `gla_site_verification`
 2. Once the `Create MC Sub-Account` button returns an `id` value, use the `Claim website` button.
     - The Create process will also return a `claim_delay` value if it performs a site verification - this is the number of seconds to wait before trying the website claim (trying sooner will return an error).

body:
This will add a new command: `markAsFailure(message)` where you can mark a test as a failure. If one run fails, all tests are marked as failed. The JSON from Browsertime (that is used in sitespeed.io) gets a failure filed and an array of failure messages (potentially you can mark a run as failed multiple times).

If we get an uncaught error when we run a tests (for example we couldn't start the browser at all), we automatically mark the test as a failure.

See https://github.com/sitespeedio/sitespeed.io/issues/3262

author: calvincarter
body:
This PR gives users the ability to create many categories and budget lines. In summary here are the changes:

1. Modified models. User can create many categories and budget lines. You will see a 1 to many relationship in each table. Also, a category can have many budget lines this is also 1 to many.
2. Moved default categories to a seeder. You can run sequelize seed to create its default data in your database. I will provide instructions on how to run and use in my PR.
3. Tested Post budgetline and categories routes. I was able to see the data appear under the user_data route. So using the /api/user_data you can see all the budgetlines and categories that user created
4. Created a new route to get default categories

Since the models have changed you will have to do the following:

1. Before starting server.js, go to the file and modify line 29 to `{force : true}`. This will drop your old db and rebuild it using the new models.
2. Once you set flag to `true`. Start the server from terminal running `node server.js`
3. Server should start without errors. Now STOP server once more.
4. Modify the server.js again and set back to false {force : false}. Why do this again? This is so that your data doesn't get wiped every time you start/stop server.
5. Run the the following to seed your database with default categories. In terminal run `sequelize db:seed:all`
```
You'll see this in your terminal if successful
Sequelize CLI [Node: 14.15.1, CLI: 6.2.0, ORM: 5.22.3]
Loaded configuration file "config/config.js".
Using environment "development".
== 20210131222736-default-categories: migrating =======
== 20210131222736-default-categories: migrated (0.005s)
```
6.  Start server running `node server.js`
7. Done. You now have default categories in your database and your tables are now up to date
